subject: ClearShip pilot: capacity probe results & enrollment checklist
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Torres <diego.torres@clearship.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: ClearShip pilot: capacity probe results & enrollment checklist

Diego — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of the operational / sizing items we agreed to validate and the immediate asks from Redwood to move the pilot to enrollment: 

Summary of what we ran (attached): clearship_probe_results.csv + sample_stream_trace.json
- Steady-state baseline: ~40 QPS (avg request payload ~420 tokens, typical response ~600 tokens).
- Microburst behaviour observed in your probe: peaks to ~250 QPS lasting ~20–40s, often correlated with batch sync windows.
- Streaming characteristics: most sessions stream ~15–60 tokens/sec after initial chunk; long-tail sessions exist (~5% > 1.5k tokens total).

Key SLO targets you stated on the call:
- Interactive latency: p95 <= 200 ms for responses up to 512 tokens (streaming enabled)
- Batch-ish windows: p95 <= 800 ms for bursts where throughput >150 QPS
- Concurrent stream count target initially: 120 concurrent streams (scale plan later)

Immediate asks / Redwood next steps (actionable):
1) We’ll size a preliminary slot plan and prewarm strategy (suggested starting point below).
2) We need a short sample of production traces with timestamps for 3 typical days (CSV or JSON), ideally with request size, response token count, and session duration (we attached a sample trace for format).
3) Confirm whether your sync windows are predictable (cron-like) or ad-hoc spikes so we can propose autoscaling windows and burst pools.
4) Procurement contact for enrollment (for Dedicated pilot paperwork).

Preliminary sizing note (informal):
- Suggested pilot pool: 6 slots (each slot ~20 QPS effective steady-state for your median payload), plus a 2-slot burst pool that can be added during sync windows (gives ~160 QPS burst headroom).
- For streaming tail protection, we recommend enabling prefix caching on identical request families and a soft-concurrency cap for long sessions (we can set defaults if you want).

Next meeting: propose Wed 05 May 10:00 PT for a short architecture alignment and procurement intro.

Attachments: clearship_probe_results.csv, sample_stream_trace.json, redwood_capacity_checklist.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the sizing spreadsheet and a formal enrollment checklist by EOD tomorrow.

— Logan Wright
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
logistics & large-scale inference
From: Diego Torres <diego.torres@clearship.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Lin <maya.lin@clearship.io>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearShip pilot: capacity probe results & enrollment checklist

Logan — great write-up, thanks. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the sample trace: 

- Request size variability: many requests are templated but we have three common templates: short-check (avg 180 tokens), routing-decision (avg 420 tokens), and full-fulfilment (avg 1,100 tokens). The probe you ran focused mostly on routing-decision; full-fulfilment spikes are less frequent but much heavier.
- Sync windows: these are mostly predictable — they happen at minute 00 of every 2 hours for regional syncs, and at 03:00 UTC for the big nightly roll (that’s when we saw the ~250 QPS).
- Streaming behavior: the stream tail you saw corresponds to long-running fulfilment conversations (customers and carriers) — those are ~5% of traffic but can persist for minutes.

Procurement: looping in Maya (ops lead) — maya.lin@clearship.io is the procurement / vendor onboarding contact. She’ll own paperwork.

We’re comfortable with the Wed 05 May 10:00 PT slot. For the sizing spreadsheet: when you say a "slot" what is the assumed GPU/memory class? If you can include the model variant (gpt-open-16k-quant or similar) and an estimated token/sec throughput per slot that will help us map to infra budgets.

Diego
Head of Platform Engineering | ClearShip Logistics
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearShip pilot: capacity probe results & enrollment checklist

Picking up a couple of technical sizing questions for Karthik to evaluate before Wed: 

Karthik — can you validate the following assumptions we used in Logan's initial note and convert them into a concrete slot plan (numbers + rationale):
1) Model choice: recommend quantized 16k-context open model variant for pilot (estimate: 350–420 tokens/sec per slot for steady streaming at 512-token responses; peak single-slot QPS will be lower for large 1,100-token responses).
2) KV cache sizing: sample traces suggest average prompt context ~1.6k tokens for routing-decision flows — confirm memory delta and whether one slot can handle 2–3 concurrent in-flight sessions with KV reuse.
3) Tail mitigation: propose a soft limit of 8 long-tail sessions per slot and a policy to shed new long sessions to the burst pool once threshold hit.
4) Autoscale windows: since sync windows are cron-like, propose scheduled prewarmed burst pool with 2x capacity for the 5-minute window around syncs.

Also note cost sensitivity: ClearShip asked us to show a conservative per-token cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated (we can produce both). If we have a rough monthly estimate for the pilot (6–8 slots steady + burst pool usage ~10% off hours) that would be useful for procurement.

I’ll compile Karthik’s numbers into the pilot enrollment checklist once we have them. Logan — please attach the sample probe CSV (from Diego) to the shared Drive folder; I added a short column mapping for the CSV fields.

— Lauren
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

See you Wednesday.

— Diego
